newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Abu Dhabi's ADCO capacity up five pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Abu Dhabi's ADCO capacity up five pct in 1996.

text.p: The Abu Dhabi Co for Onshore Oil Operations (ADCO) lifted its 1996 sustainable capacity by 55,000 barrels per day (bpd), a five percent increase over the previous year's levels, the company's annual report said.

"In 1996, sustainable capacity increased by 55,000 barrels per day (five percent), reflecting the Bu Hasa North and Bab North pressure maintenance gas injection projects which came on stream during the year," it said.
ADCO is the country's largest operator with an output of about one million bpd. The report said 35 wells were drilled during the year, including two exploration wells.
ADCO's activities centre on the producing Bab, Bu Hasa, Asab, Sahil and Shah fields.
The Abu Dhabi government owns a 60 percent stake in ADCO with the remaining equity owned by foreign firms.
British Petroleum, Shell, Total, Exxon, Mobil and Partex are shareholders.
